---
title: "Finding-Forward Headline with a Number or Clear Comparison"
author: "Your Name"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %b %Y')`"

snapshot: true

# --- Series identity (drives the utility bar across the top) ---
snapshot_label: "Empirical Snapshot"
snapshot_number: "000"
snapshot_topic: "Topic"
snapshot_util_left: "Queens College · CUNY"
# snapshot_util_right: "SCF 2022"   # optional; adds "· SCF 2022" at far right

# --- Featured figure (fills the right column) ---
snapshot_feature: "figures/placeholder-image.png"
snapshot_feature_label: "Fig. 1"
snapshot_feature_caption: "One brief line: measure, population, source, year."
# snapshot_feature_height: "4.3in"   # default cap; lower it if the sheet spills
#
# The plate is capped by height AND width, whichever binds first. Landscape
# figures (~3:2) fill the column best; a 3:4 portrait renders at ~95% width.
# Do NOT hardcode a background. Export both variants in one call:
#   hflsnap::hfl_save_figure(fig, "figures/fig1.png", width = 4.2, height = 5.6)
# -> figures/fig1.png     (bone)  point snapshot_feature here
#    figures/fig1-web.png (white) upload this one to WordPress
# Add hflsnap::hfl_watermark() as the LAST element of the ggplot chain, after
# any complete theme. Let snapshot_feature_caption do the labelling -- drop
# title/subtitle from the ggplot itself, or they duplicate the caption.

# --- Author box ---
snapshot_byline_name: "Joseph Cohen"
snapshot_byline_title: "Associate Professor of Sociology"
snapshot_byline_affiliation: "City University of New York, Queens College"
snapshot_byline_link: "jncohen.commons.gc.cuny.edu"
# snapshot_byline_bio: "Researches household finances"
# snapshot_author_image: "images/author.png"   # else a monogram disc is drawn
# snapshot_author_initials: "JC"

# --- Provenance (the footer) ---
snapshot_switch_section: 3
snapshot_license: "cc-by-4.0"
snapshot_data_note: "Data: Survey of Consumer Finances <jncohen.commons.gc.cuny.edu/scf>"
snapshot_code_url: "github.com/jncohen/your-file.Rmd"
# snapshot_tiles: ["GitHub", "SCF", "CC BY"]

# --- Masthead + type scale (all optional; defaults hold one page) ---
# snapshot_wordmark_size: "15pt"   # the HF square follows automatically
# snapshot_title_size: "21pt"
# snapshot_lede_size: "8.4pt"
# snapshot_body_size: "8.0pt"
# snapshot_body_leading: "11.2pt"

abstract: |
  Write the lead in one short paragraph: the finding, its magnitude, who is affected, and why it matters.

# fontset/accent are intentionally unset: the snapshot layout supplies the HFL
# faces (Bricolage / Archivo / Spline Sans Mono) and defaults the accent to
# vermilion E5402A. Setting accent here would override it.
fontpath: fonts/
numbersections: false
doublespace: false
linenumbers: false
maincolumns: 1

# Standalone: needs only rmarkdown + pandoc + XeLaTeX + snapshots.tex + fonts/.
# hflsnap::hfl_use() copies those files into this project folder for you.
# For the WordPress companion as well, use:  hflsnap::render_snapshot("this-file.Rmd")
# (or, without the package: source("render-snapshot.R"); render_snapshot("this-file.Rmd"))
output:
  rmarkdown::pdf_document:
    template: snapshots.tex
    latex_engine: xelatex
    keep_tex: true
    keep_md: true        # .knit.md feeds the WordPress companion
---

<!-- Snapshots are one-page public documents. Keep the writing tight, plain, and finding-centered. No subtitle, no methods section, no abstract heading. -->

<!-- Anything written here, above the first heading, becomes the opening
     paragraph of column 1, directly under the lede. -->

# Context

<!-- 130-165 words. Name the social or institutional context that makes this empirical finding relevant. -->

# Finding

<!-- 150-175 words. Explain the main result with concrete numbers and one visual. The featured visualization is set in YAML. -->

# Implication

<!-- 75-100 words. State what the finding suggests for practice, policy, or future research without overclaiming.

     Section 3 is where the body switches to column 2, under the figure --
     that's snapshot_switch_section: 3 in the YAML. Keep three sections, or
     move the switch if you change the structure. -->
